weapons.name: Terra Blade
weapons.source: Crafted from True Excalibur and True Night's Edge
weapons.why: This is the defining melee weapon of the phase because its ranged slashes stay powerful without forcing reckless positioning.

weapons.name: Death Sickle
weapons.source: Dropped by Reapers during a Solar Eclipse
weapons.why: The wall-piercing scythe projectiles make this one of the best event-farm melee payoffs before Plantera.

weapons.name: Chlorophyte Saber
weapons.why: If you want a simpler ore-route upgrade, the leaf projectile gives this a strong all-purpose boss profile.

weapons.name: Chik
weapons.source: Crafted from late pre-mech yoyo upgrades
weapons.why: Yoyo-focused melee players can keep that subclass online here instead of fully abandoning it for swords.

armor.name: Chlorophyte Armor
armor.why: The leaf crystal bonus and strong baseline stats make this the most broadly useful pre-Plantera melee set.

armor.name: Turtle Armor
armor.source: Crafted from Turtle Shells and Chlorophyte Bars
armor.why: If you want the tankiest route into the Jungle, this is the defensive ceiling before Plantera.

armor.name: Hallowed Armor
armor.why: The dodge proc still gives it real value if your Chlorophyte route is not ready yet.

accessories.name: Fire Gauntlet
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: This is the best melee accessory of the phase because it stacks several offensive bonuses into one clean slot.

accessories.name: Mechanical Glove
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: It is both a real accessory in its own right and the natural stepping stone toward Fire Gauntlet.

accessories.name: Avenger Emblem
accessories.source: Combined from a class emblem and mech-boss materials
accessories.why: A universal damage boost stays useful no matter which exact melee weapon family you lean into.

accessories.name: Mid-Hardmode Wings
accessories.source: Crafted or obtained from established Hardmode wing routes
accessories.why: Flight is still mandatory because Jungle movement and Plantera prep punish grounded loadouts.

accessories.name: Ankh Shield
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: Debuff immunity and knockback protection are especially comforting once Jungle enemies and events get more chaotic.

accessories.name: Star Veil
accessories.source: Crafted from Cross Necklace and Star Cloak.
accessories.why: Longer invincibility after a hit, plus retaliating falling stars.

buffs.name: Flask of Ichor
buffs.why: The defense reduction is too strong to ignore, which makes this the best melee weapon imbue for the phase.

buffs.name: Ironskin Potion
buffs.why: Even with stronger armor, the baseline defense boost is still valuable in every meaningful fight.

buffs.name: Endurance Potion
buffs.why: Damage reduction remains one of the best ways to make difficult Jungle and event attempts more forgiving.

buffs.name: Wrath Potion
buffs.why: A direct damage increase helps shorten fights where melee still has to spend time in danger.

weapons.name: Megashark
weapons.source: Crafted from the Minishark, Illegal Gun Parts, Souls of Might, and Shark Fins
weapons.why: This is the workhorse ranger gun for the entire stretch because it gives reliable pressure in nearly every fight.

weapons.name: Chlorophyte Shotbow
weapons.why: Bow builds get a clean burst-fire upgrade here, especially when paired with strong arrow choices.

weapons.name: Daedalus Stormbow
weapons.why: Even after mech progression, the arrow-rain pattern still solves several large-target encounters elegantly.

weapons.name: Uzi
weapons.source: Dropped by Angry Trappers in the Hardmode Jungle
weapons.why: If you farm it, the fire rate gives gun ranger another elite option before Plantera.

armor.name: Chlorophyte Armor
armor.why: The armor stats and leaf crystal bonus make this the cleanest general pre-Plantera ranger set.

armor.name: Hallowed Armor
armor.why: The dodge effect still earns this a place when survivability matters more than a pure offense step.

armor.name: Titanium Armor
armor.why: It remains a valid carry-over if you want to delay the Chlorophyte grind a little longer.

accessories.name: Sniper Scope
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: This is the premium ranger accessory here because it boosts ranged performance while also improving target control.

accessories.name: Ranger Emblem
accessories.source: Dropped by the Wall of Flesh
accessories.why: A direct ranged-damage boost is still an easy slot-in when your weapon options are already strong.

accessories.name: Magic Quiver
accessories.source: Dropped by Skeleton Archers
accessories.why: Bow-focused ranger builds still feel the damage and arrow-speed bump immediately.

accessories.name: Mid-Hardmode Wings
accessories.source: Crafted or obtained from established Hardmode wing routes
accessories.why: Ranger uptime depends on movement consistency, and this phase keeps punishing grounded play.

accessories.name: Ankh Shield
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: Debuff immunity is particularly welcome once Jungle enemies start layering crowd-control on top of boss pressure.

accessories.name: Star Veil
accessories.source: Crafted from Cross Necklace and Star Cloak.
accessories.why: Longer invincibility after a hit, plus retaliating falling stars.

buffs.name: Archery Potion
buffs.why: The research consistently calls this out as the best dedicated ranger buff in the phase.

buffs.name: Ammo Reservation Potion
buffs.why: Ammo efficiency matters once your best ammo types and long boss attempts start stacking up in cost.

buffs.name: Ammo Box
buffs.why: It is effectively free ranged value before any important fight and stacks nicely with the potion support.

buffs.name: Endurance Potion
buffs.why: Even ranged builds benefit a lot from damage reduction once the Jungle starts punishing mistakes harder.

weapons.name: Rainbow Rod
weapons.source: Found through Hallowed progression sources and Hardmode exploration
weapons.why: Its controllable projectile path makes it one of the most dependable single-target mage tools before Plantera.

weapons.name: Crystal Serpent
weapons.source: Caught by fishing in the Hallow
weapons.why: It remains an elite carry-over because the split projectile still scales well into this phase.

weapons.name: Magnet Sphere
weapons.why: The lingering sphere gives mage another way to keep damage flowing while repositioning aggressively.

weapons.name: Sky Fracture
weapons.source: Crafted from Light Shards, Souls of Light, and the Magic Missile
weapons.why: It is still a respectable burst option if you want a craftable spell that rewards good aim.

armor.name: Chlorophyte Armor
armor.why: This is the most straightforward high-end magic armor step before Plantera because it is sturdy and broadly effective.

armor.name: Hallowed Armor
armor.why: The dodge effect is still strong when you care more about safety than pushing fully into Chlorophyte.

armor.name: Forbidden Armor
armor.source: Crafted from Forbidden Fragments and Adamantite or Titanium Bars
armor.why: The hybrid identity keeps it relevant if your build likes mixing in summon support or event mobility.

accessories.name: Celestial Emblem
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: It is the cleanest mage accessory upgrade here because it boosts damage while smoothing mana utility at the same time.

accessories.name: Celestial Cuffs
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: The mana-on-hit effect helps salvage otherwise doomed attempts when a boss pattern catches you.

accessories.name: Mana Flower
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: Auto-potions reduce cognitive load and keep your strongest spells online more consistently.

accessories.name: Mid-Hardmode Wings
accessories.source: Crafted or obtained from established Hardmode wing routes
accessories.why: Flight still buys mage the room it needs to cast safely through difficult Jungle and event movement.

accessories.name: Ankh Shield
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: Debuff immunity is a real quality-of-life and survivability gain once the Jungle starts stacking status effects.

accessories.name: Mana Cloak
accessories.source: Crafted from Mana Flower and Star Cloak.
accessories.why: Auto mana potions plus a defensive star burst when you take a hit.

buffs.name: Magic Power Potion
buffs.why: It remains the most direct and valuable magic buff you can bring into this phase.

buffs.name: Mana Regeneration Potion
buffs.why: Longer fights and higher-tier spells both make mana sustain more important than it was before.

buffs.name: Crystal Ball
buffs.source: Placed station buff from the Wizard
buffs.why: It is free pre-fight magic value, so there is little reason to skip it once available.

buffs.name: Ironskin Potion
buffs.why: Mage still benefits from a simple defensive floor because burst damage remains a constant threat.

weapons.name: Optic Staff
weapons.source: Crafted from Black Lenses, Hallowed Bars, and Souls
weapons.why: This is the premier summon of the phase because the twin minions stay aggressive and versatile across boss and Jungle encounters.

weapons.name: Sanguine Staff
weapons.source: Dropped by Dreadnautilus during Blood Moon fishing
weapons.why: It remains a very strong carry-over if you already invested in the Blood Moon fishing route.

weapons.name: Firecracker
weapons.why: The tag explosion keeps this whip relevant well past the point where many earlier summon tools drop off.

weapons.name: Durendal
weapons.source: Crafted from Hallowed Bars and Souls of Might
weapons.why: Its faster whip cadence makes it a reliable alternative if you prefer smoother direct control over bigger explosions.

armor.name: Spider Armor
armor.why: Until post-Plantera armor opens up, this is still the cleanest dedicated summoner set for raw minion throughput.

armor.name: Hallowed Armor
armor.why: The dodge bonus gives it a niche if you want more personal survivability while keeping summon support online.

armor.name: Forbidden Armor
armor.source: Crafted from Forbidden Fragments and Adamantite or Titanium Bars
armor.why: It stays a viable hybrid route if your build wants a little more flexibility than pure summoner gear provides.

accessories.name: Summoner Emblem
accessories.source: Dropped by the Wall of Flesh
accessories.why: This is still the easiest and most efficient direct summon-damage upgrade available in the phase.

accessories.name: Pygmy Necklace
accessories.source: Bought from the Witch Doctor
accessories.why: An extra minion slot remains one of the highest-value single accessory effects a summoner can get.

accessories.name: Mid-Hardmode Wings
accessories.source: Crafted or obtained from established Hardmode wing routes
accessories.why: You still win summon fights by staying alive long enough for minions and whips to do their work.

accessories.name: Feral Claws
accessories.source: Found in Jungle chests or Jungle Crates
accessories.why: The whip speed boost remains a simple but noticeable improvement to the part of summoner gameplay you actively pilot.

accessories.name: Ankh Shield
accessories.source: Combined at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: Debuff immunity and knockback protection reduce the number of runs that fall apart to messy Jungle attrition.

accessories.name: Star Veil
accessories.source: Crafted from Cross Necklace and Star Cloak.
accessories.why: Longer invincibility after a hit, plus retaliating falling stars.

buffs.name: Summoning Potion
buffs.why: An extra minion is still the single best buff you can bring to a summoner loadout in this phase.

buffs.name: Bewitching Table
buffs.source: Placed station buff from the Dungeon
buffs.why: It stacks perfectly with your potion support and should be part of every serious summon setup.

buffs.name: Ironskin Potion
buffs.why: Summoner is still fragile enough that the universal defense potion remains mandatory in practice.

buffs.name: Endurance Potion
buffs.why: Damage reduction buys the breathing room you need while your minions and whips ramp up real damage.
